name: New Jersey

statute.readVia: https://codes.findlaw.com/nj/title-39-motor-vehicles-and-traffic-regulation/nj-st-sect-39-3-74/ (current as of 2024-01-01; summarized, short quote only)

statute.cite: N.J.A.C. 13:20-1.1 to 1.8 (sunscreening regulation, per MVC form MR-15)

windshield.strip: No aftermarket tint/non-transparent material on the windshield without a medical exemption; with exemption, only above the AS-1 line

frontSide.note: No aftermarket non-transparent material/sunscreening on front side windows (medical exemption only)

backSide.note: 39:3-74 restricts only windshield, wings, deflectors, side shields, corner lights and front side windows; no limit stated for rear side windows

tint.certificateOrSticker: Medical exemption: temporary approval (MVC Sunscreening 2, valid 60 days) then permanent approval document (MVC Sunscreening 4, valid 48 months) to be kept in the vehicle and shown to police and at inspection

medicalExemption.text: Windshield and/or front side windows only with MVC medical exemption, approved before installation. Application 'MVC Sunscreening 1' with physician section and valid prescription, sent to SUNSCREENING@mvc.nj.gov or Customer Advocacy Office, PO Box 403, Trenton NJ 08666-0403; install at a licensed sunscreening facility; renew every 48 months. MR-15 form lists qualifying conditions (polymorphous light eruption, persistent light reactivity, actinic reticuloid, porphyrias, solar urticaria, lupus erythematosus).

penalty.text: Fine not stated in 39:3-74 as read; unauthorized sunscreening is 'subject to removal, fines and failure to pass New Jersey inspection' (MVC MR-15)

quotes: No person shall drive any motor vehicle with any sign, poster, sticker or other non-transparent material upon the front windshield, wings, deflectors, side shields, corner lights adjoining windshield or front side windows of such vehicle
You may have your vehicle windshield and/or front side windows tinted (sunscreened) in New Jersey with a medical exemption only.
All medical sun-screening materials must be applied to the portion of the windshield above the AS-1 line. (MR-15)

helmet.conditions: All motorcycle operators and riders (fully enclosed autocycles excluded)

handheldPhone.fineText: $200-$400 first offense, $400-$600 second, $600-$800 third+ (possible 90-day suspension and 3 points)

radarDetector.note: No state ban found; commercial vehicles over 10,001 lb banned federally (49 CFR 392.71)
